body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

  Cluster-to-cluster replication currently relies on mTLS for securing the connection but has no support for JWT-based authorization. There is already existing support for JWT-based auth in client to server communication and this could be extended to include server-to-server communication.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

  Add support for JWT-based authorization on the replication stream between Temporal clusters. The replication stream already connects through the frontend gRPC server, which has a stream authorization interceptor capable of validating JWT tokens. The receiving side is largely in place. The primary gap is the ability to inject a token on the sending side.

  Key requirements:
  - A configuration option to attach a JWT to outbound replication connections
  - Per-remote-cluster token configuration, consistent with how TLS is already configured per cluster
  - Wildcard matching in the config similar to https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/issues/9881

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

  - mTLS only (current state) — Provides transport-level authentication but no authorization capabilities. Cluster trust is all-or-nothing.
  - Custom authorizer with mTLS certificate inspection — Could derive permissions from client certificate subjects, but encoding authorization claims in certificates is operationally cumbersome and doesn't support dynamic permission changes without reissuance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            

**Additional context**

  - The existing JWT claim mapper accepts tokens without an exp claim, which is relevant for long-lived replication streams, though supporting token refresh would be recommended.
  - JWT tokens for replication could carry namespace-scoped permissions in the future, enabling per-namespace replication authorization (this might require substantial changes and is likely out of scope of v1).
  - The disableStreamingAuthorizer dynamic config flag controls whether the frontend's stream authorization interceptor is active. Since replication streams don't carry tokens today, existing users may have this set to true. This interaction should be documented.
title: Add JWT support for s2s communication/replication
